orientation: A twelve-clip, four-utterance pool produced six natural expressive readings across all utterances, but every natural clip was labeled with disbelief and none was neutral-only. The pool expands the expressive gallery but cannot support the intended balanced neutral-versus-expressive retrieval test.
finding: The candidate pool supplied natural expressive coverage across new lexical content but failed to supply the neutral class required for balanced held-out retrieval.
limitations: The pool contained twelve clips from one speaker, model, and shared seed.
This was corpus construction rather than an instruction-following or retrieval evaluation.
Recipe identity was hidden, but annotation established an imbalanced realized label distribution.
negative_evidence: Only six of twelve clips met the naturalness floor.
No natural clip was neutral-only, blocking the planned balanced retrieval test.
evidence_quotes: Six met the 4/5 naturalness floor, spanning all four new utterances.
Every natural clip carried a disbelief label; none was neutral-only.
The pool successfully expanded the natural expressive gallery across new lexical content, but it cannot support a balanced held-out neutral-versus-expressive retrieval test.
